newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Renewed Wall Street strength boosts Europe.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Renewed Wall Street strength boosts Europe.

text.p: European stock markets rose strongly on Monday, enjoying renewed enthusiasm as Wall Street opened with a burst of strength.

German shares ended floor trade more than 1.2 percent higher and continued to make ground in later screen-based business. britain's blue-chip FTSE 100 index drove through 3,900 and within a few points of its trading record, while French shares went back above 2,000 points.
As Wall Street opened with a 30 point rise within the first few minutes of trade, European bourses responded by marking share prices higher.
Worries about the prospects for U.S. interest rates following jobs data released on Friday appeared to calm as markets priced in a likely 0.25 percentage point rise in rates later this month.
"The Street is becoming convinced the Fed's going to tighten rates and an increase of 25 basis points is built in," Larry Wachtel of Prudential Securities in New York said.
An attempt by the dollar to test higher levels spluttered out amid talk of sizeable sell orders and the currency slipped to around 109 yen and 1.4900 marks.
"The dollar is facing a brick wall on the top which makes it look unlikely that it will break out of the current range in the near-term," said Steve Barrow, economist at Chase in London.
By 1400 GMT the dollar was at 1.4900 marks and 109.00 yen, down from 1.4913 marks and 109.32 yen in late European trade on Friday.
Europe's financial markets have been kept cautious by the prospect that the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise rates when the Federal Open Market Committee next meets on September 24.
Any rise should help the dollar but is likely to weigh on stock markets because investors might be tempted to switch out of equities and into bonds.
British stocks bounced higher at the start and got another boost from producer price data showing benign inflation and Wall Street's strong start.
Broadly in-line price data helped soothe concerns about British inflation and kept alive speculation about the possibility of another cut in interest rates.
"Excellent figures, particularly impressive when you bear in mind several adverse factors, notably the rise in global oil prices," Mark Hale of Sakura Finance said about the data.
Bullishness over shipping group P&O's container merger with Nedlloyd and BTR's disposals programme helped push the FTSE 100 up by 19 points to 3,912.5 by 1400 GMT.
Germany's DAX index of blue-chip shares ended bourse trade just off session highs, but rose gain in post-bourse screen trading.
Shares in car-maker Volkswagen closed seven marks higher at 555.25 marks after a weekend German press report that it planned to boost its meagre return on sales.
Deutsche Bank, still suffering image problems after last week's temporary suspension of dealing in three of its British-based funds, traded 39 pfennigs weaker at 71.89 marks.
French stocks inched higher through the day, buoyed by firm bond prices and buying interest in the shares of companies involved in mergers or reporting good results.
Canal Plus was up on its merger plan with Nethold, while Cerus rose on a report of buyout talks with CGIP.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4900 marks and 109.00 yen, compared with 1.4913 marks and 109.32 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index was up 19.5 points at 3,912.5.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 31.73 points, or 1.26 percent, at 2,548.73. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index was up 9.87 at 2,552.61.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 17.55 at 2,022.30.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $384.60 against $385 in the morning and $385.50 at Friday's London close.
